title: GAP – Geriatrics, Activity, Prevention Use of Orthelligent® VISION for the early detection of fall risks
summary:
Limited mobility and an increased risk of falls are common problems among older adults. These are often caused by age-related changes as well as disorders of the nervous system, muscles, or musculoskeletal system. Changes in gait patterns or recurrent falls can provide important indications of such conditions. Therefore, it is essential to detect fall risk early and reliably.
Early assessment of fall risk is important not only for the health of affected individuals but also for society as a whole. Preventing falls can help avoid injuries, improve quality of life, and reduce healthcare costs. New technological developments, such as digital applications and artificial intelligence, offer new opportunities to objectively assess fall risk over extended periods.
With the help of video recordings and specialized software, movements can be analyzed automatically. Parameters such as step length, walking speed, asymmetries, and joint movements can be measured precisely. However, AI-based systems have so far been tested primarily in healthy individuals. It therefore remains unclear whether they function reliably in older adults with health impairments.
A key question is whether AI-supported methods can meaningfully complement or potentially even replace existing approaches for assessing fall risk.

interventions.name: Patients aged 65 and older undergoing inpatient rehabilitation are assessed at the beginning of the rehabilitation program and again at the end (after 3 weeks) using movement analysis as well as standardized clinical geriatric assessments.
Healthy individuals aged 65 and older are assessed once using movement analysis and standardized assessments.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients undergoing inpatient treatment in the geriatric trauma department of the BG Unfallklinik Murnau.
Patients are able to understand the study and provide written informed consent.
Gait and balance analysis as well as fall risk assessments using Orthelligent® are performed at admission and at discharge.
The “Identification of Seniors At Risk” (ISAR) score is used to classify patients into the different groups.
Exclusion criteria:
Neurological disorders (for the comparison cohort)
BMI ≥ 31 kg/m²
Gait speed < 0.5 m/s
Delirium, identified by a positive Nursing Delirium Screening Scale (Nu-DESC) score
Dementia, moderate or severe cognitive impairment, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) < 24
